recognize_zh: 兩顆巨大細胞各含 4 個彼此分離、大小一致的圓至卵圓形細胞核，細胞質豐富呈藍灰色帶細小顆粒、邊緣不規則，這是蝕骨細胞（osteoclast），而非核融合分葉的巨核細胞。
features: Two giant multinucleated cells, each with about four separate, uniform round-to-oval nuclei
Nuclei are discrete (not interconnected lobes) with fine chromatin and small nucleoli
Abundant blue-gray cytoplasm with fine azurophilic granules and irregular frayed borders
No platelet budding from cell margins
Background erythrocytes, a neutrophil and a few myeloid cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows two large multinucleated cells, each containing several separate, uniform, round nuclei set in abundant finely granular blue-gray cytoplasm with irregular borders. The nuclei do not overlap or connect as a single lobulated mass, and there is no platelet budding. These features identify osteoclasts, which should not be confused with megakaryocytes.

ddx.vs: Megakaryocyte nuclei are lobulated and interconnected into a single polyploid nucleus with pink granular cytoplasm, rather than multiple discrete round nuclei.
Osteoblasts are mononuclear with an eccentric nucleus and a perinuclear hof, often in clusters, not giant multinucleated cells.
Carcinoma cells form cohesive clusters of separate cells with pleomorphic nuclei and distinct cell borders, not a single cytoplasmic syncytium with uniform nuclei.
Histiocytic giant cells usually have vacuolated or phagocytic cytoplasm and occur with granulomatous inflammation; morphologic overlap may require clinical context.
